plan.title: Consumer deft binary rejects colon-namespaced policy verbs that AGENTS.md tells consumers to run

narratives.Description: Consumer `deft` rejects colon-namespaced policy verbs such as `policy:show` that AGENTS.md documents as runnable commands. Disclosures often print `task policy:…`, which widens the mismatch. This story registers policy:* colon aliases in packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts (mirroring triage:*) and aligns disclosure strings so documented forms match the binary.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Consumer `deft` rejects colon-namespaced policy verbs (`policy:show`, etc.) that AGENTS.md documents, while disclosures print `task policy:…`. Register `policy:*` colon aliases in dispatch.ts (same pattern as triage:*) and align disclosure strings.

## Acceptance

- `deft policy:show` (and documented policy:* forms) resolve like `deft policy show`
- Disclosure/remediation strings match what the binary accepts
- Tests cover the alias path
- Closes #2367
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts: register colon aliases for policy:* verbs (policy:show, policy:allow-direct-commits, policy:enforce-branches, policy:enable-value-feedback, and any other policy subcommands documented in AGENTS.md) mirroring TRIAGE_ACTION_ALIAS_SUBCOMMANDS injection pattern — map policy:show → argv ['policy','show',…] so consumer `deft policy:show` works. 2. Update policy disclosure / remediation strings that print `task policy:…` to be binary-aware (deft vs task) or dual-form so AGENTS.md examples match what the binary accepts. 3. Tests covering deft policy:show (and at least one other policy:* alias) exit path. 4. CHANGELOG + Closes #2367. Prefer aliases over rewriting AGENTS.md away from colon forms (issue allows either; aliases match existing triage pattern and keep docs stable).
narratives.UserStory: As an operator following AGENTS.md, I want `deft policy:show` and other documented policy:* colon forms to work on the consumer binary, so that documented commands match what the CLI accepts.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a built consumer deft binary, when `deft policy:show` is invoked, then it resolves like `deft policy show` and does not reject the colon form as an unknown verb.
Given documented policy:* forms (allow-direct-commits, enforce-branches, enable-value-feedback), when invoked with colon syntax, then they map to the policy module subcommands.
Given policy disclosure/remediation strings, when printed, then they use forms the binary accepts (deft and/or dual deft/task), not task-only colon forms that confuse consumers.
Given dispatch tests, when they run, then they cover at least `policy:show` and one other policy:* alias exit path.
